question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code with the -p flag to review each pull request. A script then posts the findings as inline PR comments. The script often fails because Claude returns the review as free-form prose. When parsing does succeed, some findings lack the file path or line number that an inline comment needs. Which changes should you make to fix both problems?

options.text: Add the --output-format json flag so that the review result comes back as machine-parseable JSON rather than prose.
options.reason: The guide names --output-format json as the CLI flag that produces machine-parseable output in CI contexts, which fixes the parsing failures.

options.text: Extend the posting script with regular expressions that pull file paths and line numbers out of the free-form prose review text.
options.reason: The guide's approach is to have Claude Code emit machine-parseable structured findings with --output-format json and --json-schema, not to parse prose in the posting script.

options.text: Add the --json-schema flag with a schema that requires file path, line number, severity, and message for every finding.
options.reason: The guide names --json-schema as the CLI flag that enforces the structure of CI output, so every finding has the fields that an inline comment needs.

options.text: Add a rule to CLAUDE.md asking Claude to write each finding as a JSON object that includes the file path and line number fields.
options.reason: The guide presents CLAUDE.md as the place for project context such as review criteria; it presents the --output-format json and --json-schema flags as the way to enforce structured output.

options.text: Remove the -p flag so that a developer can check the format of the review interactively before the script posts any comments.
options.reason: The guide says -p is needed in CI to run non-interactively and to prevent hangs on interactive input, so removing it breaks the automated pipeline.
